---
title: Choose Query Shape and Loading
---

# Choose Query Shape and Loading

Choose result shape and relationship loading independently, then add targeted
relationship paths when needed.

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-cap: "Choosing RECAP query shape and relationship loading"
flowchart TD
    Start[What data does the task need?]
    Start --> Identity{Identity and scalar fields only?}
    Identity -->|Yes| Ref[Reference results: ref shape, no relationship loading]
    Identity -->|No| Full[Complete schema results]
    Full --> Complete{Need complete relationship tree?}
    Complete -->|Yes| Eager[Complete tree: eager loading]
    Complete -->|No| Targeted[Targeted loading with explicit includes]
    Targeted --> Bounded[Use explicit relationship paths or descendants]
```

References cannot use relationship loading. Choose references when identity and
scalar fields are enough. Otherwise choose a full shape, then use eager loading
for a complete relationship tree or non-eager explicit includes for targeted
relationships. Explicit includes require a full shape with non-eager loading.

## Choose a result shape

`shape="ref"` returns lightweight identity-oriented models. `shape="full"`
returns complete schema models.

```python
references = namespace.query_maker().resources(shape="ref").all()
resources = namespace.query_maker().resources(shape="full").all()
```

Use references for identity, IDs, and scalar fields. Use full models for schema
fields and relationship access.

## Choose loading mode

`load="none"` avoids relationship hydration. `load="eager"` loads the
configured relationship tree.

```python
minimal = namespace.query_maker().resources(shape="full", load="none").all()
complete = namespace.query_maker().resources(shape="full", load="eager").all()
```

Use eager loading only when the complete tree is required. For a bounded
subtree, prefer explicit inclusion or `descendants()`.

## Include targeted relationships

`include(...)` selects explicit relationship paths on full, non-eager queries.
Convenience methods expand to those paths:

```python
resources = (
    namespace.query_maker()
    .resources(shape="full", load="none")
    .include(["template", "properties", "children"])
    .all()
)

runs = (
    namespace.query_maker()
    .process_runs(shape="full", load="none")
    .include_steps(include_parameters=True)
    .include_resources()
    .all()
)
```

`include_template()` is the resource shortcut. Process runs provide
`include_steps()` and `include_resources()`.

## Invalid combinations

Relationship loading is unavailable for references. These combinations raise
`ValueError`:

```python
namespace.query_maker().resources(shape="ref", load="eager")
namespace.query_maker().resources(shape="ref").include("template")
namespace.query_maker().resources(load="eager").include("children")
```

Use `shape="full", load="none"` with `include(...)`, or use
`shape="full", load="eager"` without explicit includes.
